title: Restriction, tensor and pullback of locally constant line powers
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], A an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and use the concrete integer and locally constant powers in [def-sfb-locally-constant-line-twist]. (1) For every locally constant d:X->Z, integer m and open U on which d=m, the restriction of A^d to U is isomorphic to the restriction of A^{tensor m}. (2) For locally constant d,e there is an isomorphism A^d tensor A^e isomorphic to A^{d+e}. (3) For any scheme map f:Y->X and any proof that f^*A is invertible, f^*(A^d) is isomorphic to (f^*A)^{d composed with f}, using the explicit pullback of [def-pc-module-pullback]. All statements include empty strata and infinitely many strata.

source.place: Tags 00AL and 00AM (gluing on disjoint opens); modules.tex Tags 01CD and 01CR (tensor pullback and invertible dual evaluation); EGA II Remark 4.2.7, integer twist convention.

proof.text: Use disjointOpenProduct_restrict for the family of integerLinePower A hA m and the degree opens of d. Distinct degree fibres are disjoint. The hypothesis d=m on U is exactly U contained in the m-th degree open, so this proves the first clause directly from the concrete product.

For d,e take the disjoint cover indexed by integer pairs (a,b), with open the intersection of their degree-a and degree-b fibres. On each intersection use the first-clause comparisons, module_pullback_tensor, and TensorInverse.addIso' a b to identify the tensor product with the sum twist. Apply disjointOpen_nonempty_iso to the resulting local isomorphisms.

Prove the integer-power pullback comparison in the assigned module. The tensor pullback unit is identified by uniqueness of adjoints with ordinary pullback of the unit. Tensor compatibility takes the inverse evaluation isomorphism to a tensor inverse for the pulled-back line. Fully faithful tensoring by that line compares this inverse with its prescribed dual. Induction on natural tensor powers then proves both nonnegative and negative integer cases.

Cover Y by the degree fibres of d composed with f. The map from each such fibre to the matching fibre in X is the morphism restriction. The restriction square commutes. Tensor pullback composition, the source restriction comparison, and the proved integer-power comparison identify both restrictions. Apply disjointOpen_nonempty_iso. This uses no arbitrary-product preservation by f.

proof_origin.place: Tags 00AL, 00AM and 04TN (disjoint gluing), Tag 0097 (pullback composition); modules.tex Tags 01CD and 01CR (tensor and invertible evaluation); EGA II Remark 4.2.7. B4 formalizes the concrete product restriction, tensor assembly, inverse cancellation and pullback gluing.

lean.statement:
theorem locallyConstantLineTwist_identities {X : Scheme.{u}} (A : X.Modules)
    (hA : A.IsInvertible) :
    (∀ (d : LocallyConstant X ℤ) (m : ℤ) (U : X.Opens),
      (∀ x : X, x ∈ U → d x = m) →
        Nonempty ((tensorPullback U.ι).obj (locallyConstantLineTwist A hA d) ≅
          (tensorPullback U.ι).obj (integerLinePower A hA m))) ∧
    (∀ d e : LocallyConstant X ℤ,
      Nonempty (locallyConstantLineTwist A hA d ⊗ locallyConstantLineTwist A hA e ≅
        locallyConstantLineTwist A hA (d + e))) ∧
    (∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ X)
      (hAf : ((tensorPullback f).obj A).IsInvertible) (d : LocallyConstant X ℤ),
      Nonempty ((tensorPullback f).obj (locallyConstantLineTwist A hA d) ≅
        locallyConstantLineTwist ((tensorPullback f).obj A) hAf (d.comap f.base.hom)))
